summary: Ordinary dispatch takes a zero-marked human/nonhuman theme, sometimes a l-marked person, plus l-goal, recipient suffix, aʕm-accompaniment, or purpose. A l-marked lexical agent can double the L-series agent ending (Mor Barsaumo /18; ezo koviye /20).
II.1a has a bəṯr-marked person to be fetched and an unexpressed messenger/message. Bare summons in Story of Dawid /7 lacks the bəṯr construction and remains 1.
Infectum-wa 60/43 is inherited and not relabeled just from retrospective German. The clearer double-L mtaráswayleli supports a separate Preterit-wa example; its segmentation still needs confirmation.
The lookup for ṭrṣ shows rolling in I/III, whereas mṭaraṣṣe in 85/8 is already trs II sending. Preserve the source consonant irregularity and entry ownership.

There is no independent new collocation established merely by xabro or maktub as ordinary dispatched themes. The corrected Infectum example is restored from supplied evidence, not replaced by a different verse.
